title: Saved lifecycle reconciliation, explicit read completion and coherent detail snapshots

discussionDecisions.reason: Visible Window focus covers visible-unfocused missing-channel returns; visible visibilitychange, persisted pageshow and stable saved-view entry cover complementary returns. No-op records/preview semantics prevent file-picker focus invalidation; no polling or localStorage mirror.
A request arriving after the initial read starts cannot be dropped when start finishes. Consume only covered requests and drain later hints even without pending writes.

Preserve complete active content identities and known-equal small metadata. Opaque archive values are not serialized/normalized to force no-op detection; conservative recovery publication must not invalidate unrelated active-record previews.

Explicit requests receive a covering accepted snapshot, promptly defer around blocked local work, fail with the real error, or stop promptly on epoch termination. One I/O owner plus request-scoped completion avoids both stale immediate results and global-idle starvation; startup connections remain owned.

Current source demonstrates the global retry-permission leak and captured-openJob/current-saved mixture. Finite per-entry attempts and origin-bound committed display snapshots correct both while preserving catalog origin and explicit new-save intent.

Fable-owned native history observation records the actual document and persisted event rather than asserting cache eligibility by intent. Literal returned state is required on the observed path; synthetic event tests remain separately identified.

Keep existing error labels, durable formats, atomic imports/recovery deletion and exact sample retirement. Successful normal writes may resume after a read, but errors and missing-record recreation remain explicitly retried.

Visible Window focus covers return to a still-visible window when channel delivery is unavailable; visibilitychange alone need not cover it. Visible visibilitychange, persisted pageshow and stable in-app saved-view entry complete the bounded signal set. Coalescing, visibility rechecks, cleanup and semantic preview identity address redundant events and file-picker return without a cooldown that loses later requests (docs/design/saved-lifecycle.md:33-40, 66-72, 98).

An initial read may cover requests known before its read boundary, but later requests must survive and drain even when no writes are pending. This resolves the startup/empty-flush gap in src/lib/saved-controller.ts:103-112 and 162; unconditional clearing at startup completion would lose an observed change. Revision02 explicitly defines both the boundary and the required handoffs (docs/design/saved-lifecycle.md:42, 47, 62).

Accept Main's explicit counterproposal to Fable's unconditional no-subscriber requirement for arbitrary recovery values. Full validated job/record equality and ordered-array reuse preserve active-data identity; occupied count and unreadable-ID membership separately govern preview validity. Whole-snapshot reuse is appropriate only when remaining state is known equal. Fresh opaque originals may conservatively notify without resetting an otherwise unchanged preview, while real recovery/error/phase changes remain visible; no archival serialization or normalization is required (docs/design/saved-lifecycle.md:66-72).

Revision02 incorporates C1-C4. Typed results plus a serialized dirty-read loop suffice with the specified per-request read coverage and accepted snapshot, prompt deferral around pending work, completion without waiting for global quiet, prompt stopped settlement independent of native completion, ownership of the startup connection, and lifetime-safe finalizers/drain handoffs. The result type or one shared idle-only Promise alone would not suffice. These requirements resolve my prior completion/start/stop blockers (docs/design/saved-lifecycle.md:42-62).

Recreation permission belongs only to retained retry entries and is consumed before one apply attempt; empty reconnect and subsequent unrelated edits receive no grant. Saved-origin detail follows the current saved posting, then retains its last committed displayed posting after removal; the explicit save callback uses that same posting/company. Exploration-origin detail retains its catalog snapshot, and pending drafts retain priority. These address both material gaps without broadening storage semantics (docs/design/saved-lifecycle.md:78-98).

The separate Fable observation browser must remove the BFCache-disabling default argument, record document identity and actual pageshow.persisted, and assert the expected current record on the path that occurred. A reload is valid evidence for the reload path only; synthetic dispatch and reload cannot establish retained-document restoration. Revision02 states this boundary and does not require an unsupported eligibility claim (docs/design/saved-lifecycle.md:115, 125).

Keep existing errors, explicit retry, transaction completion, atomic import checks and precise recovery targeting. Reconciliation uses the established SavedStore.read, including atomic sample retirement, so unconditional zero-mutation assertions would be incorrect. Normal pending writes may proceed through a successful handoff, while failed writes remain protected from automatic retry or recreation. No schema, mirroring or persistent-draft rewrite is needed (docs/design/saved-lifecycle.md:48-51, 58, 62, 76-86).

My proposal excluded Window focus for two reasons: a read on return from the native file picker, and read cost. The first is removed by the semantic identity rule (contract lines 66-70) so an unchanged read cannot mark a review stale or restart comparisons. The second does not outweigh the correctness case Main/Astra identified: a visible but unfocused window whose channel is unavailable gets no visibilitychange when the user clicks into it, so only Window focus can reconcile it. Window focus in the bubble phase does not fire for element focus moves inside an already focused window, which makes 'focusing the saved search box causes no read' a testable gate. In-app entry closes the persistent-App gap: App.tsx:107-111 and 139-142 change view without any read today. No polling, online, or localStorage ping agreed; my own Q2 recommended the same.

This corrects my Q4. start() assigns this.store only after the initial read resolves (saved-controller.ts:101-108); a refresh() during that window records refreshRequested and returns (260-262); start() then calls flush(), which exits at 162 with an empty queue, so the hint is stranded until unrelated later activity. A hint known before the initial read began is covered by that read, but one arriving after the read captured its snapshot can describe a newer commit and must drain after acceptance even with zero pending writes. Clearing the flag at the end of start(), as I suggested, would lose exactly that second case. Both branches are deterministic with a gated initial read and a read-count spy.

Accepted as a refinement of my D3, not a lowering. Every user-visible outcome I proposed depends on preserved job, record, and records-array identity plus the dialog comparing occupied and unreadable-ID membership, not on a zero-subscriber-call proxy: Views.tsx:54-66 memoizes on saved identity, usePostingStatus.ts:72-95 keys its effect and WeakMap on saved and job identity, SavedDataDialog.tsx:71 compares the records array. legacy and additional-legacy originals are strings (saved-store.ts:220, 226), so an exact no-op is cheap there and remains required: same snapshot object and no subscriber call when recovery is empty or string-only. retired-samples and unreadable-record originals are fresh opaque objects on each read (221-222); a conservative publish there has no visible effect because the active array identity is kept, and it must not be suppressed when the archive really changed (older-tab sample rewrite yields count 2). Tests assert both the strict case and the conservative case explicitly.

Typed completion with covering-read semantics is the smallest fix for F3: today an explicit compare during an active read resolves immediately (260-262) and refreshReview announces a comparison against whatever getSnapshot() returns afterwards (SavedDataDialog.tsx:114-119, useSavedJobs.ts:38). Prompt deferred, rather than awaiting a pending or failed write, keeps the existing gated-write and import tests (saved-controller.test.ts:103-117, 219-239) free of deadlock and keeps the writer priority at 275-279. Prompt stopped settlement and ownership of the startup connection are needed because start() holds opened locally (101-107) and stop() (120-127) cannot close it; a late success must be observed but never published into the new epoch. All of refreshed, deferred, failed, and stopped are deterministic with gated store wrappers and a close spy; E2E covers the refreshed and failed paths.

F5 is source-backed and I missed it in my own review: retry() sets recreateMissing unconditionally (211), the only reset is inside the flush loop (182), flush() returns early with an empty queue (162), and a later update then hands its draft to store.apply (169), which recreates an externally removed record without the missing error (saved-store.ts:252-255) and without the explicit restore choice promised at SavedStorageNotice.tsx:15. Per-entry, per-attempt permission consumed when the authorized apply begins, with no grant from an empty-queue reconnect and no inheritance by new operations, is finite and testable. The detail scope is likewise source-backed: App.tsx:68-72 captures openJob, :104 looks up savedOpenJob, :321 renders match from openJob while note/status come from the current list and onToggleSave saves openJob. Binding saved-origin details to the current record, keeping exploration-origin catalog content, retaining the last displayed S2 after external removal, and saving S2 from the same displayed match is coherent and checkable with literal titles and URLs.

I will execute it as a case inside the agreed E2E file using a separately launched, owned Chromium (ignoreDefaultArgs removing --disable-back-forward-cache, same channel as the config), the existing fixture server on the owned loopback origin, no real collection, browser closed in finally with its PID recorded. Evidence per attempt: a document token set after load, a pageshow listener writing event.persisted to both a window field and sessionStorage, the navigation entry type and notRestoredReasons where exposed, and CDP Page.backForwardCacheNotUsed reasons when not restored. Token retained and persisted true is classified as native restoration; anything else is labeled a reload path and never counted as restoration. On either path the returned current note committed while away is asserted literally. The production fixture serves index.html with Cache-Control no-cache (default-e2e-server.ts:60), which does not itself block BFCache; eligibility with an open IndexedDB connection and BroadcastChannel is environment-dependent and will be recorded, not claimed.

Matches my D2, D4, D6, and D7. My optional InvalidStateError remap is withdrawn, so the read-failure E2E asserts the existing texts: title '저장소 연결을 확인해 주세요.', help '저장소에 연결하지 못했거나 저장이 중단됐어요. 다시 시도해 주세요.', suffix ' 마지막으로 읽은 기록을 표시하고 있어요.' (SavedStorageNotice.tsx:27, 16, 40). Zero-mutation assertions install counters only after ready and only in fixtures without sample entries, because read() retires samples inside a readwrite transaction (saved-store.ts:203-207, 92-106) and the first open of a fresh profile writes meta once (189). Handing off to already-pending successful writes after a read is normal flow; a failed write is attempted again only through the explicit retry button.

limits: All added postings, notes, import files and provider responses used for regression execution are synthetic. This stage does not crawl new jobs, confirm current real-world openings or measure production API load.

Most visibility, focus and persisted-pageshow scenarios dispatch controlled events or instrument the test document. They prove the specified handler and state behavior, not operating-system tab scheduling. The separately recorded native history trip uses a real browser navigation and is classified only from its correlated trusted evidence.

A native reload is not evidence of BFCache restoration. The observed path for each selected run is recorded explicitly; this single Chromium build, launch configuration and trip do not establish restoration eligibility across browsers or future sessions.

The 320px screenshots use an emulated viewport in Chromium rather than a physical mobile device. Finite race scenarios and the 500-record case are regression coverage, not exhaustive scheduling or responsiveness benchmarks.
Pending failed input remains in the current tab and is exportable; this change does not make unsaved drafts durable across closing the tab or implement same-field collaborative conflict resolution.
The CLI records claude-fable-5-1 responses and a requested max effort; backend effective effort is not exposed. Astra was requested as global.openai.gpt-6-astra with reasoning max.
Point-in-time owned power assertions plus filtered Sleep/Wake/DarkWake records support the selected execution windows; they are not continuous operating-system instrumentation.
Unanimous approval is a decision to proceed on the reviewed source and evidence. It does not assert that untested browsers, schedules or data are defect-free.

The four actual failed-draft timelines start after the failed write and layout readiness. At sampled T0 the focused field is already partly behind/below the footer; the sampled T1/T2 focus, field/dialog position and scroll agree. Ordinary later scrolling exposes the required targets. These discrete endpoints cannot exclude transient movement or reflow between samples, establish a pre-T0 cause or prove automatic initial visibility. Endpoint arithmetic supports a matching net content offset only. No capture-only or product-defect cause is inferred.

Each final still records one framed state with valid measured endpoints, not continuous layout visibility. Import captures follow an explicit return from the functionally asserted page2 to page1. Detail header/lower frames share the same record state while description expansion and scrolling change layout; href values come from actual assertions/state, not readable URL pixels.
